verdict.rationale: SavvyCal ships a documented REST API. It covers core scheduling operations: listing, creating and cancelling events, updating and duplicating links, and fetching available slots. Webhooks and an MCP integration for managing links are also documented. Nothing documents that the API matches the UI, and many UI features (meeting polls, workflows, Stripe payments, round-robin configuration, branding) have no API endpoints in the evidence. Probes also found no published OpenAPI spec. Missing for 10: an explicit API/UI parity claim, API coverage of polls, workflows, payments, round-robin and branding settings, a published machine-readable spec, and independent corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: The SavvyCal API adheres to REST conventions.
List events GET /v1/events ... Cancel event POST /v1/events/{event_id}/cancel ... Create event POST /v1/links/{link_id}/events
Update a scheduling link PATCH /v1/links/{link_id} ... Duplicate a scheduling link POST /v1/links/{link_id}/duplicate
Connect Claude, ChatGPT, Cursor, VS Code, or another MCP client to check your calendar, find open times, book meetings, and manage your links from a chat.
